ns2:group.ns2:description: What good is a vaccine people don't trust? Immunologist and TED Fellow Kizzmekia Corbett co-developed the first COVID-19 vaccine to enter clinical trials — but she says making the vaccine was never the hardest part. The real obstacle is the gap between scientists and the people who have honest questions about the shots they're being asked to take. She shares a refreshing approach for taking on vaccine inquisitiveness and ensuring that humanity is ready for the next pandemic.

Apple’s HomeView smart display is the centerpiece of its new push into the home. There’s plenty to like, but also some drawbacks. It’s an extension of your iPhone or iPad with access to your texts, calendar, and reminders, making it a communal device with personal content, but switching between the two is where HomeView stumbles. The $299 display brings Siri AI to a multipurpose screen designed to manage your smart home and make everyday tasks easier. Charlie Deets is a product designer at The Browser Company, where he works on Dia. Window management on hyper-key quadrants, notes and dictation a keystroke away, switching Dia tabs through Raycast instead of the browser's own UI, and the menu bar replaced by commands. He finishes with clipboard history, Raycast on Windows for gaming, and the personal to-do app he built as an extension.

All children develop at different paces — so why do schools expect every student to learn the same way? Early education researcher Anna Rainio introduces "playworlds," a learning activity where adults and kids create imaginary stories together. She shows how pretend play helps students find their place — and the power of a teacher or parent starting with a simple question: Why not? (Recorded at Play@TED on May 14, 2026)

ns2:group.ns2:title: The New Standard Paris: Raycast, Linear and Mistral on building software with agents
ns2:group.ns2:description:
The New Standard came to Paris. Thomas (co-founder and CEO of Raycast), Tuomas (co-founder and CTO of Linear) and Théo (VP of Engineering at Mistral) talk with Tanguy, Raycast's very first angel investor, about how software gets built now that agents write so much of the code: shipping without human review, what stays off-limits to agents, building for agents, craft and quality, team shape and hiring, and what they'd do differently. Then an open Q&A with the audience.
The New Standard is our event series on how tech, product and design are changing, after San Francisco, New York and London. Thanks to Linear for co-hosting, and to everyone who came.
